AUTHORITY RULE (content-system/brand/voice-guide.md 'Write with authority'): no research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, trace or confirm; our sources or method; what the internet says; myths sections; 'you will often read'). Topic: the bridal veil. The title promises meaning and why: state an origin, date or meaning as fact ONLY where a fact gives it. Faith and cultural uses (e.g. the Jewish bedeken; Christian, Hindu or Muslim ceremonies) only where sourced and tied to their tradition. Otherwise show what couples do today, confidently (who lifts it, wearing it back, heirloom veils, choosing not to wear one).

Likely sections (brief finalises): why brides wear veils today; the veil in ancient Rome (flammeum) only as sourced; medieval and religious veiling as sourced; the Victorian white veil (e.g. Queen Victoria's lace) as the V&A or Royal Collection Trust describe it; royal veils as official pages describe them; the veil in faith traditions as sourced; lifting the veil; blusher, wearing it back and heirloom veils; choosing a veil for a destination (wind, heat, beach or clifftop) as practical points; travelling with a veil; choosing not to wear one.

Sources: V&A, Royal Collection Trust (rct.uk), the Met Costume Institute, Britannica, Oxford Reference (folklore dictionaries), official or academic faith sources (e.g. Jewish institutions), academic dress-history sources. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs, bridal retailers or Wikipedia.
